text: The proposal is not a business row. It is a view of the local decision record answered on API-S4-003 GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}, with the proposed step, the reasons (rule ID, condition and facts), the cost and effect with its source, the deciding role and the package version. The step vocabulary is a versioned reference value whose content is not published, and the cost and effect are read on rwb-agent's contract under DP-20 with the rule as fallback. No sixth REST operation is added to the five of TSD S4 T-A.1 and `legal_action` gains no column.
why: No owned table of this service carries a recommendation, no owned operation proposes a step, and the FSD names the Model gateway as an integration point without naming an operation; declaring a column or a sixth operation would break the ownership rows and the boundary the checks enforce, and writing the steps as an enumeration would put a business value in the code.

confirm: Solution architect of S4 with the P10 architect and the business owner of S4
impact: If the proposal must be stored, `legal_action` gains a recommendation reference and the DB story of this service changes; if the agent row becomes a C dependency, only the Dependency Map and the metadata rows change. The rule evaluation, the record and the answers do not change.

text: TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN, PACK_COMPLETE and SETTLEMENT_PROPOSED are read as the names of workflow signals and state-machine events, not as Kafka subscriptions. The pack-complete and template-withdrawn signals are raised by this service's own pack and defect-list steps and delivered to LitigationWorkflow; the officer task, the case-stage timer and the case move are answered to rwb-case in one stage outcome; the generation hold is answered to rwb-comms with the rule and its version. This legacy key publishes and consumes no event.
why: The FSD describes the trigger as 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer' and the rules name an event per outcome, while the ownership rows give rwb-litigation zero events, the FSD declares no background event and DP-09 is not in the pattern set; a consumer or a producer invented here would put a topic, an inbox and an event catalogue entry into a service the ownership map gives none, and the task and timer rows are P3's.

text: The template status of R-LIT-04 is read on rwb-comms' notice contract as part of the notice answer, and the pack index of R-LIT-16 is read on rwb-document's contract with its defect list items. Both elements and both operation names carry the placeholder. When one of the two facts is absent the rule does not fire, nothing is written, no move is answered and the case keeps its state.
why: The template status has no field identifier in the notice row the legacy table names only in part, and the pack index has no published element at all, while TSD S4 T5.2 gives documents to P5 and Architecture v5 slide 10 gives notices to P6; inventing a field or a status value would create a reference no owner approved and would put a business value in the contract.
